savings.reason: Reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full): sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13792 with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 8(a) saves only statutory agency authority; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; nothing is transferred. Own-residual check, reading EO 13792 in full: it orders a review of national monument designations and two reports and creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 3(c) disclaims rights); it designates, modifies and withdraws nothing itself. Any later Presidential proclamation about monument boundaries was a separate act under the Antiquities Act, and EO 13990 sec. 3 reviews those proclamations on its own terms, so none is a surviving effect of this order. research_rationale: EO 13792 (signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431), read in full from the held FR text, orders the Secretary of the Interior to review Antiquities Act monument designations made since 1996 (sec. 2(a)-(c)) and report to the President, an interim report within 45 days and a final report within 120 days (sec. 2(d)-(e)). The machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)) and condition (sec. 3(b)). A report deadline is never an end; the order has no sunset or termination wording, so every clause remains part of the order until revoked. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked on the report-deadline question; the producer does not claim when either report was delivered. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20. The dossier lists no missing provision and no other actor provision; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13792 named only in EO 13990. The monument-boundary proclamations of 2017 were separate Presidential acts, not part of this order. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. Inventory: the dossier's 18 clauses cover the operative text from sec. 1 through sec. 3(c); its scope labels for sec. 2(a)(v)-(vii) ('sec2-v', 'sec2-v-vi', 'sec2-v-vii') are irregular but each span is correct and no text is missing or duplicated.
